title: A Colony for the Signal Anew
premise: Dominic Coldharbour smuggles memories between the two halves of a sundered human fleet, the Waking and the Sleeping, whose truce expires in ninety days. When a manifest lists a passenger aboard a ship that was scrapped decades ago, he discovers a hidden cryo-ark holding the fleet's original founder, whose waking would legitimize one faction and doom the other. Torn between his loyalty to the smugglers' guild that raised him and the truth he owes both worlds, Dominic must choose which half of humanity wakes first. He wakes neither: he broadcasts the founder's own recorded testimony to both fleets, forcing them to end the truce not with war but with a shared reckoning.
about_author: Wren Fairweather is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests before writing stories about what ships carry. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and excellent coffee, and write about people who move things they shouldn't.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Running contraband memories past orbital customs on the long route between the Waking and Sleeping fleets, he finds an impossible name on his manifest: a passenger aboard the Meridian, a ship scrapped forty years ago. The beat is unease — the routine job that stops being routine.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashback. He traces the ghost entry to a decommissioned drydock and meets Ilsa Vane, a guild archivist who reveals the Meridian's true cargo: a hidden cryo-ark holding the fleet's founder. Beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Debt
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She explains the schism — the Waking who kept flying, the Sleeping who chose cryosleep rather than surrender their claim — and why the founder's awakening would crown one side. Beat: the weight of history pressing on the present.

chapters.title: Contraband Hearts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Smuggling a memory-capsule for a Sleeping family, he falls for Captain Sera Okonkwo of the customs cutter assigned to catch him — a woman who knows exactly what he is. Beat: love kindling inside opposition, duty sharpening against desire.

chapters.title: The Guild's Price
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvo's POV. The guild learns of the ark and orders Dominic to deliver it to the Waking council as payment for old protection. Beat: betrayal looming; loyalty revealed as a debt with interest.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aboard her cutter, she intercepts Dominic but lets him pass, then discovers her own orders: if the truce expires without resolution, she is to fire on the ark. Beat: duty curdling into horror; she warns him at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What the Founder Knew
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Inside the ark, he plays the founder's final memory-log and learns the schism was engineered by the founder herself to force humanity to choose its future consciously. Beat: revelation that reframes everything — truth cuts both ways.

chapters.title: The Run to Drydock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Dominic and Sera. With the guild hunting him and the Waking fleet mobilizing, Dominic runs the ark toward neutral space while Sera defies her orders to shield him. Beat: full-throttle rising action; love openly declared against duty.

chapters.title: Truce Expiring
chapters.summary: Climax. Multiple POVs converge at the ark: Corvo's enforcers, Sera's mutinous crew, the Waking vanguard. Dominic broadcasts the founder's testimony to every ship in range, forcing both fleets to hear the truth simultaneously. Beat: the choice made — no side wakes first; all wake together.

chapters.title: A Colony for the Signal Anew
chapters.summary: Resolution, Dominic's POV. The fleets stand down into a joint tribunal; the guild fractures, and Corvo faces judgment. Dominic and Sera, both stripped of rank, pilot the first sanctioned ferry between the halves. Beat: quiet hope — memory shared instead of smuggled, a colony founded on signal rather than silence.
